## Code Style and Conventions

### General Guidelines
- Write clean, readable, and maintainable code
- Follow language-specific best practices and idioms
- Keep functions and methods focused on a single responsibility
- Use descriptive variable and function names
- Add comments for complex logic, but prefer self-documenting code

### Naming Conventions
- Use clear, descriptive names that convey intent
- Follow the naming conventions of the primary programming language used
- Avoid abbreviations unless they are widely recognized

### Code Organization
- Keep related functionality together
- Maintain a logical project structure
- Separate concerns appropriately

## Testing

### Test Coverage
- Write tests for new features and bug fixes
- Ensure tests are meaningful and cover edge cases
- Keep tests focused and independent

### Test Structure
- Follow existing test patterns in the repository
- Use descriptive test names that explain what is being tested
- Group related tests together

## Documentation

### Code Documentation
- Document public APIs and interfaces
- Keep documentation up-to-date with code changes
- Use inline comments sparingly and only when necessary

### README and Guides
- Keep the README.md current with project status
- Document setup and installation procedures
- Provide usage examples where appropriate

## Version Control

### Commits
- Write clear, concise commit messages
- Make atomic commits that represent a single logical change
- Reference issue numbers in commit messages when applicable

### Branches
- Use descriptive branch names
- Keep branches focused on specific features or fixes

## Security

- Never commit sensitive information (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- Follow security best practices for the technologies used
- Validate and sanitize user inputs
- Keep dependencies up-to-date

## Dependencies

- Only add dependencies when necessary
- Prefer well-maintained, popular libraries
- Keep dependencies up-to-date
- Document why specific dependencies are needed

## Code Review

### Before Submitting
- Test your changes thoroughly
- Ensure code follows project conventions
- Update documentation as needed
- Check for any unintended changes

### Review Process
- Be respectful and constructive in reviews
- Focus on code quality and maintainability
- Suggest improvements, not just identify issues

## Performance

- Consider performance implications of code changes
- Optimize when necessary, but prioritize readability
- Profile before optimizing
- Document performance-critical sections

## Accessibility

- Follow accessibility best practices
- Ensure features are usable by all users
- Test with various input methods and assistive technologies
